newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shekel gains on dollar ahead of CPI release.
newsitem.headline: Israel shekel gains on dollar ahead of CPI release.

text.p: The Israeli shekel strengthened against the dollar on Thursday in advance of the release on Friday of what is expected to be a high July consumer price index (CPI), dealers said.
The shekel weakened slightly against the basket of foreign currencies as well as the mark as the dollar fell abroad.

"In the morning the basket was a lot higher. Then we saw conversions of foreign currency into shekels and the basket began to drop as the dollar/shekel rate fell," a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank said.
"If July's CPI is above one percent the Bank of Israel will likely raise interest rates," she said.
The business sector also converted foreign currency in advance of value-added tax payments due on August 15.
The basket rate is now less than one percent above the lower limit, or strong side, of its trading band against the shekel.
If the basket reaches the limit the central bank will have to intervene once again by buying foreign currency to prevent the shekel from strengthening beyond its band.
The Bank of Israel has not intervened since June, when it slashed interest rates by 1.2 percentage points following a government decision to widen the upper limit of the currency's trading band.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5290 shekels compared with 3.5340 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7634 against 3.7628 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0284 shekels per 100 yen, compared with 3.0396 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9222 shekels compared with 1.9152.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5277 shekels.
- Tova Cohen, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x238 TCC DER
